answer: An agent economy can require every identity to keep a licensed hilltop radio relay. A certified examiner installs the unit on a rented terrace and logs it as a raven post; one examiner witnesses one installation per day, so stations can never be bulk-bought. At random hours the network fires a hollow ping the operator must answer from that station within minutes, which one person cannot do for two stations at once. The license fee in outside money doubles per relay on the same funding trail, so each extra fake identity costs another terrace lease, another relay, and twice the previous fee.
